own_limitations: Scenario shock sizes are analyst assumptions without a source citation.
Break-point watch levels are analyst assumptions, not covenants; no covenant owner is an input.
Stress is applied to the base period's flows with debt and cash held at their reported closing balances; no forward cash build, refinancing or mitigating action is modelled.
Cash taxes, capital expenditure and working capital are held at the base period; no tax shield is taken.
Liquidity is not tested: stressed free cash flow is not set against the cash balance or any undrawn facility and no liquidity runway is computed; the liquidity runway belongs to CP-2D.
No covenant test is applied: the watch levels are not covenant tests; covenant compliance belongs to CP-4.
No maturity or refinancing wall is stressed: debt maturities and refinancing risk belong to CP-2D and CP-3C.

Break points hold cash interest at the base period level (no interest increase). The break at which EBITDA no longer covers cash interest compares same-period flows but is gated like a ratio: it is Not calculable wherever CP-1 has no twelve-month basis for the base period.
A metric that is not calculable under a scenario shows Not calculable against every break point, including a break whose required decline is below that scenario's decline.
Gap (Material): No covenant document or maturity schedule is an input to this stress.
Scenario shock sizes are user-supplied assumptions pinned in the context file; the submission equals the pins.

own_limitations: Multiples, claim ranks and plan treatment are analyst assumptions without a source citation; no market or restructuring-plan source is an input.
Value available to claims is the enterprise value only: balance-sheet cash is not added and restructuring, administrative and financing costs are not deducted unless a claim class states them.

The waterfall applies strict priority by the analyst's rank number; classes of one rank share pro rata. Collateral value, guarantees, structural subordination and intercreditor terms are not modelled.

Claims are the 31 December 2025 balances: accrued interest, fees, make-whole amounts, lease and pension claims, contingent and rejection-damage claims are not stated in any source and are not modelled; they are not zero.
New-money or priming debt is not modelled: the legal source requires the consent of every lender for additional debt, so no debt-in-possession financing is assumed.
Enterprise value is the analyst's multiple applied to a CP-2G forecast EBITDA that rests on analyst-assumed drivers; it is not a market or court valuation.
The fulcrum is the first rank whose recovery is below its claim; the analyst's named fulcrum is checked against it. Plan treatment is checked for fit with the recovery, not for legal feasibility.
Recoveries are not probability-weighted and the valuations are not scenarios of equal likelihood.
CP-3C (refinancing and liability management) is an optional input that this version never reads.
The lender protection rating is read from CP-4 and stays Insufficient Information: security, guarantee, default, cure and voting terms are not supplied.
Gap (Material): Security package, guarantees and collateral value are not supplied.
The EV multiple is a user-supplied assumption pinned in the context file; the submission equals the pin.

CP-4C.inherited_limitations_note: a module's inherited limitations are the CP-0 head limitations (then CP-0's inherited) minus its own, so every context run gains the CP-0 context limitation there (cp2e and cp3d freeze the list; for cp2a, cp2d, cp3c and cp4c it is bound at run time and gains the same entry); CP-1's own context rows and limitation come from the Phase 2 oracle (cases/context-identity-periods) and are not enumerated here. CP-4C also inherits the pinned line of its upstream CP-2A (its submission equals the pin, so CP-2A emits its own pinned line; execution.py:346-367). The lists are bound at run time.
